title: Causa Rellena
subtitle: cold layered potato cake filled with tuna and avocado
excerpt: Causa rellena is a Peruvian cold dish made from seasoned mashed potato layered around a filling of tuna, mayonnaise and avocado. It is assembled in a mould and chilled before serving as a starter. The potato layer is flavoured with aji amarillo paste and lime juice.
sourceNotes: Causa comes from the Quechua word 'kausay', meaning life or sustenance. The dish was eaten by Peruvian independence fighters who used the potato as a base. Today causa rellena is served as a cold starter in homes and restaurants across Peru and is a showcase for the country's extraordinary potato variety.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be assembled up to a day ahead and kept covered in the fridge.

content.text: This recipe serves 6 as a starter and takes about 50 minutes of active work plus 1 hour of chilling time. You boil and mash 1kg of floury potatoes while they are hot, then season the mash with aji amarillo paste, lime juice and oil. This potato layer becomes the base and lid for a filling of tuna, mayonnaise and sliced avocado.

The potato must be mashed while it is still hot and worked until very smooth with no lumps. If it cools before mashing it will become gluey and hard to work with. A loaf tin or individual ring moulds both work well for shaping. Line the tin with cling film so the causa lifts out cleanly.
Peel and boil 1kg floury potatoes in salted water until completely tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and mash immediately while hot. Push through a ricer for the smoothest result.

While the potato is still warm, work in the aji amarillo paste, lime juice, vegetable oil and a generous pinch of salt. Mix until evenly combined. Taste and adjust seasoning. Set aside to cool to room temperature.
Drain 2 tins (160g each) of tuna in oil. Mix with 4 tbsp mayonnaise and the finely diced onion. Season with salt.
Line a loaf tin or deep dish with cling film, leaving enough overhang to fold over the top. Press half the potato mixture in an even layer on the base.
Spread the tuna mixture over the potato layer in an even layer. Lay the avocado slices over the tuna.
Press the remaining potato on top, smoothing with the back of a wet spoon. Fold over the cling film and press gently to compact the layers. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
When ready to serve, lift the causa out of the tin using the cling film. Slice into portions and garnish with black olives. Serve cold.

attrs.symptom: Potato layer is sticky and hard to press into the tin
attrs.cause: The potato cooled too much before the oil was worked in
attrs.fix: Season and mix the potato while it is still warm. If it has cooled, briefly warm it in a saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly, before using.

attrs.cause: The causa was not chilled long enough to set
attrs.fix: Chill for a full hour minimum, or overnight. Compact firmly when assembling and always cut with a sharp knife.

attrs.cause: The avocado was cut too far in advance and exposed to air
attrs.fix: Slice the avocado just before assembling the causa. A squeeze of lime juice over the slices also helps slow browning.

content.text: Causa rellena is a popular starter at Peruvian family gatherings and is often the first dish on the table at celebrations. It is made ahead and served cold, which makes it easy to prepare for a crowd.
